meta.universe: Top-level comments on the monthly 'Ask HN: Who is hiring?' thread, 2011-04 to the latest thread. YC-adjacent startups, NOT the US labour market.
bias: Hacker News 'Who is hiring?' is a BIASED sample: YC-adjacent startups and remote-friendly software companies, not the US labour market. Nothing here generalises to a BLS total.
Thread volume is a popularity signal, not a hiring signal: 10,259 postings in 2021 against 2,644 in 2026. Use shares; never plot raw counts as demand.

PARTIAL years must be marked wherever they appear - see partial_years and months_per_year. 2011 starts at the first thread (2011-04) and the latest year runs only to the newest thread, whose own month is still live.
Technology and role shares are share-of-postings, not share-of-mentions.
445 comments could not be confirmed as job ads and were dropped, so per-year posting counts are a floor, tightest in 2011 and the latest year.
The remote classifier scores 92.9% on a blind held-out set. 'unknown' is kept as its own class and is never folded into onsite.

misclassified.text: Dave.com is hiring senior engineers in LA.
Hall, now in SOMA is hiring. Learn more about our move: https://hall.com/blog/hall-headquarters-move-to-san-francisc...
Roadie | Multiple Positions | Full-time, Fully Remote | Atlanta Based | https://www.roadie.com

classifier.note: heldout_blind_sample is the honest generalisation estimate: 42 header strings drawn at random (one comment per thread, seed 20260902) and hand-labelled BEFORE the classifier was run on them. curated_hard_cases was assembled after reading the corpus and only verifies that the intended rules fire.

taxonomy_notes: Every pattern is a Python regex applied case-INSENSITIVELY unless a part of it is wrapped in (?-i:...), which makes that part case-sensitive.
A technology is accepted when one of its `patterns` matches and no `anti_patterns` match overlaps that match.
A technology flagged `ambiguous` additionally needs, within 90 characters of the surviving match, either an accepted unambiguous technology or a word from _qualifier_pattern.
A technology with a non-null `requires` additionally needs that regex to match within 250 characters of the match ('Phoenix' only counts near Elixir; 'Lambda' only near AWS).
Matching runs on the cleaned posting text with URLs stripped, so a technology name that only appears inside a link does not count.
A posting counts at most once per technology however many times it names it.

schema.shares: shares are NOT shipped as separate arrays: divide any *_counts array by the matching totals array. count/total reproduces the share the source file publishes exactly. A zero denominator means null, not 0.
schema.remote_totals: postings in the strict 'remote' class per month / per year - the denominator for tech.year_counts_remote read as 'share of remote postings', and NOT the denominator for 'remote share of postings mentioning X' (that one is tech.year_counts).

definitions.universe: Top-level comments on the monthly 'Ask HN: Who is hiring?' thread, 2011-04 to the latest thread. YC-adjacent startups, NOT the US labour market.
definitions.share: share of ALL postings in that year - denominator = signals.totals.postings. A posting counts once per technology however many times it names it.
definitions.remote_share_of_tech: rem = remote postings mentioning the technology / ALL postings mentioning it, that year (rem_n / rem_d). 'remote' is the strict fully-remote class only: the HN technology series carries no hybrid breakdown.
definitions.remote_share_of_role: rem = fully-remote postings in that role / all postings in that role; remhyb additionally counts the hybrid class. Denominator is the role's own posting count, not all postings.
definitions.min_support: a technology is reported only when it has at least 40 postings in 2018 or in 2025. Raw counts (n0, n1) ship with every row so a 2 -> 6 move cannot masquerade as a trend. Roles are never dropped, but low_support marks the thin ones.
definitions.ci95: 95% normal-approximation interval on the share DIFFERENCE of two independent proportions. HN is a convenience sample, not a random one, so read this as a noise floor, not a confidence statement about the labour market.
definitions.counts_warning: Thread volume fell from 10,259 postings in 2021 to 2,644 in 2026 (partial). Counts are NOT a hiring indicator; only shares are.
